body:
I write this not as the tripper, but as a DanceSafe NYC volunteer who helped save the tripper's life. My name is Kevin, and Allison is a fellow DanceSafe member.
I was sitting in a stairwell giving my friend a massage, and suddenly Allison runs down toward me. 'Kevin,' she says, 'tell me everything you know about AMT.'
I immediately knew something awful was happening, and told her as much as I could rattle off. She told me to meet her by the coat check in ten minutes. I plow through the sweaty hordes of ravers to find out more about this situation. Apparently there were reports of a 17yo kid shouting obscenities, being violent, and convulsing that Allison immediately responded to.
I get a look at the kid, sitting in a cold stairwell, sweating bullets. He can't make eye contact, is trying desperately to escape the restraining arms of his friends. He is shouting randomly and is not responding to his name. '5-MeO-AMT overdose,' I conclude. I asked his friends what he took, and they '5MEMT' so I had some decent confirmation. Apparently he had snorted an unknown amount that was meant to be ingested. I recognized his state from a trip report I had read on Erowid and knew that he wasn't just having a bad trip - he needed to be hospitalized.
According to his friends, he had been having a relatively normal trip for 6 hours before he started acting violent. One of his friends remarked that he had personally snorted the same amount and felt no effects. Another friend claimed that he believed the tripper snorted 5x an oral dose, which leads me to believe that either nobody really has any idea what they were talking about, or they thought they were dealing with AMT. The information is very sketchy.
We reached a consensus and Allison called the ambulance while I instructed his friends very carefully what they must do.
I grabbed a piece of paper and wrote, 'NO ANTIPSYCHOTICS.' Tryptamine overdoses are usually shot up with Haldol or Thorazine, leaving the poor psychonaut with weeks of hell and cognitive impairment. 'BENZODIAZEPINES OKAY.' I was very clear that this information must get to the hospital workers, and Allison wrote down '5-MeO-AMT - see erowid.org.'
The party got shut down when the police rolled up, we were thanked and left. Allison got a call from the kid's friends. Remarkably, they treated him just like I recommended. We heard from his friends when he was in the hospital, and I just heard from another one a few minutes ago. He's home right now, sleeping. No word on possible brain damage.
Our unfortuante tripper is another example of an insufflation casualty. The message is very clear - snorting 5-MeO-AMT usually ends in disaster, and doing drugs without the education to accompany it even moreso.
